question: The FEC row stores dielectric 78.4 at 296.15 K (23 C) on the authority of Kobayashi et al. 2003 Table 2, whose FEC row carries footnote e. A peer-reviewed downstream paper, Nanbu et al. 2007, restates the same number (and the same viscosity) as 40 C while citing that same Kobayashi paper. Does any primary source support 40 C, and does the competing 107 leg carry a temperature that would let the two legs be reconciled as a temperature pair?
answer: No on both counts. (1) The 40 C restatement has no primary support: Nanbu et al. 2007 recasts the same cited values as 40 C, and it does so for two quantities at once (dielectric 78.4 and viscosity 4.1 mPa s), so the conflict is a systematic temperature shift in a downstream citation rather than a second measurement. Re-reading the primary table visually at 600 dpi confirms the FEC row carries superscript e on the 4.1 and the 78.4 entries and that footnote e reads "At 23 C."; the neighbouring EC row carries footnote c "At 40 C". The primary therefore governs and T_K stays 296.15 K. (2) The competing 107 leg is quoted downstream with a near-room temperature, not a different one: two open J-STAGE papers state "about 107 at 25 C" for FEC and both attribute that number to Hagiyama et al. 2008, the same Chem. Lett. paper the dataset already names. The two legs therefore sit at essentially the same temperature (23 C vs 25 C) and remain an unreconciled value conflict. Nothing is averaged, nothing is promoted, and model_ready stays false.

primary_source.citation: Kobayashi, M.; Inoguchi, T.; Iida, T.; Tanioka, T.; Kumase, H.; Fukai, Y. Development of direct fluorination technology for application to materials for lithium battery. J. Fluorine Chem. 2003, 120(2), 105-110.
primary_source.table: Table 2, Physical properties of non-fluorinated and fluorinated carbonates

footnotes_verbatim.b: Physical properties are cited from ref. [11,12] except our data.

primary_source.verification_method: The table page was rendered at 600 dpi with PyMuPDF and inspected as an image, because a purely textual extraction cannot be trusted for superscript footnote markers. The rendered row shows 4.1^e, 78.4^e and 1.04^e and the rendered footnote block shows "e At 23 C."
primary_source.temperature_of_the_stored_value: 23 C = 296.15 K, carried on the cell itself by footnote e
primary_source.provenance_marker: The FEC row ends in 'Our data', i.e. the authors measured it; footnote b reserves the cited columns for the [11,12] rows.

declared_conflict.citation: Nanbu, N.; Suzuki, K.; Yagi, N.; Sugahara, M.; Takehara, M.; Ue, M.; Sasaki, Y. Use of Fluoroethylene Carbonate as Solvent for Electric Double-Layer Capacitors. Electrochemistry 2007, 75(8), 607-610.
declared_conflict.verbatim: The dynamic viscosity of FEC (4.1 mPa s at 40 C)4) is higher than those of EC (1.930 mPa s at 40 C)12) and PC (2.530 mPa s at 25 C).12) Strange to say, the relative permittivity of FEC (78.4 at 40 C)4) is lower than that of EC (89.78 at 40 C).12) The relative permittivity of PC is 64.92 at 25 C.12)
declared_conflict.verbatim_note: Extracted with PyMuPDF; the earlier plain-text extraction of this PDF carried a broken font encoding that hid all numeric strings, which is why this quote could not be probed until the page was re-extracted.
declared_conflict.its_reference_4: M. Kobayashi, T. Inoguchi, T. Iida, T. Tanioka, H. Kumase, and Y. Fukai, J. Fluorine Chem., 120, 105 (2003).
declared_conflict.its_reference_12: J. A. Riddick, W. B. Bunger, and T. K. Sakano, Organic Solvents: physical properties and methods of purification, 4th ed., Wiley-Interscience, New York (1986).
declared_conflict.is_an_independent_measurement: no - reference 4 is the same Kobayashi 2003 paper the dataset already cites, so this is a downstream restatement, not a second experiment
declared_conflict.scope_of_the_shift: the restatement moves both the dielectric constant (78.4) and the dynamic viscosity (4.1 mPa s) of the same molecule from 23 C to 40 C at once
declared_conflict.what_it_does_not_establish: it does not establish a 40 C measurement, and it is not a source of the 107 value either; the 107 line runs through Hagiyama 2008

sources.citation: Nambu, N.; Takahashi, R.; Takehara, M.; Ue, M.; Sasaki, Y. Electrolytic Characteristics of Fluoroethylene Carbonate for Electric Double-Layer Capacitors at High Concentrations of Electrolyte. Electrochemistry 2013, 81(10), 817-819.
sources.verbatim: The relative permittivity of FEC (about 107 at 25 C)5 is considerably higher than that of PC (64.92 at 25 C).6
sources.its_reference_5: K. Hagiyama, K. Suzuki, M. Ohtake, M. Shimada, N. Nanbu, M. Takehara, M. Ue, and Y. Sasaki, Chem. Lett., 37, 210 (2008).
sources.verbatim_note: whitespace-normalised: the source breaks the line between "(about" and "107 at 25 C)5"; the cell content and order are verbatim, not the native byte sequence

sources.verbatim: The relative permittivity of MetPC (about 102 at 25 C)4 was also considerably higher than that of PC (64.92 at 25 C)5 and was comparable with that of FEC (about 107 at 25 C).4
sources.its_reference_4: K. Hagiyama, K. Suzuki, M. Ohtake, M. Shimada, N. Nanbu, M. Takehara, M. Ue, and Y. Sasaki, Chem. Lett., 37, 210 (2008).

competing_leg_temperature.same_reference_item_as_the_dataset: yes - both 2013 papers name Hagiyama et al. 2008, Chem. Lett. 37, 210-211, which is the paper the dataset already names as the unread primary candidate behind the 107 leg
competing_leg_temperature.status: read at secondary level only; Hagiyama 2008 itself is still not held locally

temperature_pairing.reading: the two legs are near-isothermal, so the 78.4-vs-107 split cannot be explained away as a temperature artefact; it stays a value conflict (frequency, purity, method or transcription) to be settled against Hagiyama 2008 or another primary source

decision.value_verdict: retain 78.4; do not move T_K to 313.15 K; do not average the two legs
decision.stored_value_unchanged: dielectric stays 78.4, T_K stays 296.15, model_ready stays false
decision.conflict_registration: the 40 C restatement is logged as a downstream citation conflict on the row (conflict_status and notes) and in the model-exclusion evidence, so a reader of the dataset alone sees it
follow_up: Reading Hagiyama et al. 2008 would settle both the existence and the conditions (temperature, frequency) of the 107 measurement, which is the only thing that can close this row.
No Kobayashi 40 C variant has been found; if one is ever produced it would have to be weighed against the primary footnote before T_K could move.
